title: The Funeral
teaser: White lilies, gold columns, a furious widow, and a will that says the crown must be chosen.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Port Harcourt. White lilies, gold columns, and three hundred mourners pretending not to watch each other.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: For the first time in years, all four houses stand under one roof.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nabyen keeps one hand in her pocket, closed tight around half a coral bracelet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tari stands at the back, still smelling of the creeks, watching the doors.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Hadiza counts the exits, then the guests, then the guards.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Kolade works the room like it's the opening of a new bank.

lines.speaker: ibiere
lines.text: Four strangers at my husband's funeral. He collected people the way other men collect cars.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A thin Englishman with rain still on his coat clears his throat. Oliver Ashworth, the family's London solicitor.

lines.speaker: oliver
lines.text: Chief Okoro left instructions. The chairmanship of Confluence Holdings, what he called the Crown of the Confluence, is not inherited.

lines.speaker: oliver
lines.text: It is chosen, by the four houses together. Once they have brought back the second half of his will from Geneva, and the last seal from his brother.

lines.speaker: ibiere
lines.text: His brother? Gideon had no brother.

lines.speaker: oliver
lines.text: He did, Madam. And the first half of the will is waiting in my office in London.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the lights die.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When they flicker back on, someone has slashed the Chief's portrait from corner to corner. Pinned to the canvas, a card in neat handwriting: 'One of you is next.'

lines.speaker: ibiere
lines.text: Who did this? WHO DID THIS?

lines.speaker: ibiere
lines.text: And this one. A trader from the hills? In my husband's will?

lines.speaker: ibiere
lines.text: Do you know what they call girls like you, Nabyen Dalyop? Gold-diggers.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: My mother dug tin, Madam. Not gold.

choices.text: Step in front of Nabyen. "Say that again, Madam. To me."

response.speaker: nabyen
response.text: ...Thank you.

response.speaker: ibiere
response.text: How touching.

choices.text: "He was my father, Madam. And I didn't come here for his money."

response.speaker: ibiere
response.text: ...Liar.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: But her face has gone grey.

choices.text: "Where were YOU the night he died, Madam?"

response.speaker: ibiere
response.text: Get out of my house.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: Three hundred people heard that. By evening, so has all of Port Harcourt.

choices.text: "We're all grieving. Let's bury him in peace."

response.speaker: ibiere
response.text: ...Fine. For him. Not for you.

choices.text: Turn the Chief's letter over and hand it to Ibiere. Pencilled on the back: 'Forgive me, Kaneng.'

response.speaker: ibiere
response.text: ...He wrote that? About her?

response.speaker: ibiere
response.text: Then he lied to both of us. Sit down, girl. You belong here more than I do.

choices.text: Quote the ledger to the whole room: GREED, circled three times in his own hand.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: Three hundred mourners go silent. Somewhere at the back, a glass breaks.

response.speaker: ibiere
response.text: Someone was robbing him. In my house.

choices.text: "He once promised me a bride from the Plateau, Madam. Did you know that?"

response.speaker: nabyen
response.text: ...Excuse me?

response.speaker: ibiere
response.text: Oh, this funeral is getting interesting.

choices.text: "My father swore an oath on the Nun River to protect him. I swear the same: I'll find who did this."

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: Old men from the creeks stand up at the back of the hall, one by one.

response.speaker: ibiere
response.text: ...Your father was a good man. Sit down, Tari.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Midnight. The garden behind the mansion, fireflies over the fountain.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the edge of the fountain, someone has left a white lily. Tied to its stem with black thread, a note.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Welcome home, little sheep. — B.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And on the bench beside Nabyen, where nobody saw it placed, a single red rose.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Breathe. I am here. — W.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the stone bench: the Chief's tea tray, taken from his study before the police arrived. One silver spoon has gone black at the tip.

lines.speaker: hadiza
lines.text: And this. Four million dollars a year into Banque Moreau, Geneva. For ten years.

lines.speaker: tari
lines.text: Moreau. The man I pulled out of the creek said a white woman was paying in francs.

lines.speaker: kolade
lines.text: Banks are boring. Let's talk about who flies to London tomorrow.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In Kolade's pocket, his phone buzzes. Geneva. He doesn't answer it.

response.speaker: nabyen
response.text: Then I'll try to deserve it.

choices.text: Tari. He's already bled for this.

response.speaker: tari
response.text: Nobody touches you while I'm breathing.

response.speaker: hadiza
response.text: Wise. Numbers don't lie. People do.

response.speaker: kolade
response.text: Finally, somebody with taste.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Later, everyone else has gone inside. Nabyen is still by the fountain, turning half a coral bracelet in her fingers.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: He was my father, you know. I never met him. I only ever saw him in newspapers.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: Do you think he was a good man?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Midnight in the garden. The air is thick with night-blooming jasmine and unsaid promises.

lines.speaker: kolade
lines.text: You shouldn't be out here alone, Nabyen. Port Harcourt is full of men who take what isn't offered.

lines.speaker: nabyen
lines.text: And are you one of them, Mr Balogun?

lines.speaker: kolade
lines.text: I prefer it when it's offered freely.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Footsteps on the gravel. Tari, watching from the path, not pretending otherwise.

prompt.text: Kolade steps into her shadow. She can feel the heat coming off his jacket.
The fireflies are very bright tonight.

choices.text: Hold his gaze and step closer. "Then make me an offer worth accepting."

response.speaker: kolade
response.text: Careful, Miss Dalyop. I might.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: On the path, Tari turns and walks away without a word.

choices.text: Press the blackened spoon into his chest. "Explain why Banque Moreau money runs through your bank."

response.speaker: kolade
response.text: ...Where did you get that?

response.speaker: kolade
response.text: Not here. This house has ears. In London, I tell you everything.

choices.text: Show her the blackened spoon. "Your father was murdered, Nabyen. I can prove it."

response.speaker: nabyen
response.text: ...Then we find who did it. Together. Promise me.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: She doesn't let go of your hand for a long time.

choices.text: Take her hand. "I think he loved you more than he knew how to say."

response.speaker: nabyen
response.text: ...You're kind. I didn't expect kind, here.

choices.text: "He was a great man. Not always a good one."

response.speaker: nabyen
response.text: Honest. I'll take honest.

choices.text: Turn to Tari. "Sit with me. Just you."

response.speaker: tari
response.text: I'll sit here until the sun comes up, if you want.

choices.text: Leave the fireflies to their silence.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: Tomorrow: London. Some conversations can wait.

outcomes.title: Blood on the Lilies
outcomes.text: You called the widow a murderer in front of three hundred people. If you're wrong, you've made a powerful enemy. If you're right, you've warned her.

outcomes.title: His Daughter
outcomes.text: Nabyen told the world whose daughter she is. There's no taking that back now.

outcomes.title: Shield of the Rock
outcomes.text: You stood between Nabyen and the widow's anger. She noticed. Everyone noticed.

outcomes.title: The Peacemaker
outcomes.text: The Chief was buried in peace. Peace is rare in this family. Enjoy it.

reflections.text: Something started by the fountain tonight.
The name Moreau keeps coming up.

s_spoon.title: The silver spoon
s_spoon.text: SPOON. The poison was never in the tea. It was on the silver spoon, a gift from Geneva, engraved 'E.M.'

m_funeral.title: White Lilies
m_funeral.text: Gold columns, three hundred mourners, and four heirs under one roof.

m_garden.title: Fireflies at Midnight
m_garden.text: A blackened spoon, a fountain, and a hand held in the dark.

k_spoon.title: The blackened spoon
k_spoon.text: Silver, engraved E.M. Gone black at the tip, the way silver does when it meets poison.

epigraph.text: Every funeral is a gathering of the people who did not do it.
